standard.title: Complex letter combinations
standard.description: understand how to use and apply phonological and morphological knowledge to read and write multisyllabic words with more complex letter combinations, including a variety of vowel sounds and known prefixes and suffixes
standard.prior_knowledge: Students apply phoneme-grapheme knowledge and syllable patterns to fluently read and write multisyllabic words (AC9E3LY09). They have not yet applied this knowledge to more complex letter combinations including a variety of vowel sounds and known prefixes and suffixes.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students can read and write multisyllabic words with more complex letter combinations — including a variety of vowel sounds and known prefixes and suffixes — by applying phonological and morphological knowledge.

nodes.label: Complex vowel sounds in multisyllabic words
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify and apply complex vowel patterns in multisyllabic words, including unstressed vowels.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify the vowel pattern in at least two multisyllabic words with complex letter combinations and read/write them correctly.
nodes.typical_width: Apply knowledge of a range of complex vowel patterns — unstressed vowels, vowel digraphs in multisyllabic words — to read and write words accurately, including words such as 'builder', 'animal', 'straightaway', 'thoughtful'.
wider: Sort multisyllabic words by vowel pattern and identify rules or generalisations that help predict spelling
Use morphological analysis to identify how vowel sounds shift across word families (e.g. explain vs explanation)
nodes.hinge_reason: Adding prefixes and suffixes in N2 requires accurate reading and writing of the base word — vowel errors in the stem produce compounded errors when morphemes are attached.

response_modes.reason: Unstressed vowels in multisyllabic words are a common source of spelling errors at Year 4. Reliable reading and writing of these patterns requires practice across many exemplars before automaticity is achieved.

success_criteria: Can correctly read at least five multisyllabic words with complex vowel combinations
Can correctly write at least five multisyllabic words with complex vowel combinations

nodes.label: Prefixes and suffixes in multisyllabic words
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify known prefixes and suffixes in multisyllabic words and use this knowledge to decode and spell them.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify a prefix or suffix in a multisyllabic word and use this morphological knowledge to read or spell the word correctly.
nodes.typical_width: Apply knowledge of known prefixes (un-, re-, pre-, dis-) and suffixes (-ful, -less, -ness, -tion, -ing, -ed) to decode and spell a range of multisyllabic words, explaining how the morpheme changes or adds meaning.
wider: Explore how the same prefix or suffix appears across multiple words from different word families and generalise about its meaning contribution
Use morphological decomposition as a decoding strategy for unfamiliar long words in subject texts

response_modes.reason: Morphological awareness grows through accumulating prefix and suffix families across contexts — each new morpheme learned expands the decoding and spelling range transferably across vocabulary domains.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Morphological awareness — understanding how prefixes and suffixes build words — is a transferable decoding and spelling strategy with genuine breadth across vocabulary domains.
success_criteria: Can identify a prefix or suffix in a multisyllabic word and name its meaning
Can use prefix/suffix knowledge to decode or spell an unfamiliar word
